questions.question: Which object-fit value ensures an image fills its assigned dimensions without stretching or distortion, cropping if necessary?
questions.explanation: object-fit: cover scales replaced content to maintain its aspect ratio while completely filling the element's box.

questions.question: What happens if both width and height are set to 200px on an image without object-fit?
options: The image is distorted and stretched to fit 200x200 if its natural ratio was not 1:1
The browser converts it to SVG
The image crops from the bottom
questions.hint: Default object-fit is fill, which distorts.
questions.explanation: By default (object-fit: fill), forcing non-proportional dimensions stretches and squashes the image.

questions.question: Which property controls the focal alignment point when an image is cropped by object-fit: cover?
questions.explanation: object-position (e.g. object-position: top center) determines the alignment of the image within its box.

questions.question: Why is aspect-ratio: 16 / 9 crucial for Web Vitals performance?
options: It reserves the exact layout slot dimensions before the image downloads, preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
questions.hint: Prevents layout shifts during image loading.
questions.explanation: aspect-ratio allows browsers to calculate the height from the width immediately, reserving layout space and preventing CLS.

questions.question: What is the universal CSS rule to ensure images never overflow their parent containers?
questions.explanation: max-width: 100%; height: auto; ensures images scale down fluidly within parent boundaries while preserving proportions.
